    Four-arrow quotient obstructions and ray valency #

    This file isolates the exact quotient-extraction input needed to turn representation-finiteness into global three-valency of a ray category. Different quotient obstructions are allowed for outgoing and incoming forks. Rigidity of irreducible ray arrows leaves two cases at either endpoint: four noncentral neighbors, or one loop and three noncentral neighbors.

    source
    structure LargeIndecomposable.HasFourRayQuotientObstruction (k : Type u₁) [Field k] (A : Type v₁) [Ring A] [Algebra k A] (C : Type w₁) [CategoryTheory.Category.{x₁, w₁} C] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms C] :
    Prop

    The exact quotient-extraction interface needed to turn representation-finiteness into the global three-valency bound. It deliberately allows different outward and inward obstruction quotients.

    • outgoing (x : RayVertex C) : 4 ≤ Nat.card (OutgoingQuiverArrow x) → ∃ (I : TwoSidedIdeal A), ¬IsRepresentationFinite k (A ⧸ TwoSidedIdeal.asIdeal I)
    • incoming (z : RayVertex C) : 4 ≤ Nat.card (IncomingQuiverArrow z) → ∃ (I : TwoSidedIdeal A), ¬IsRepresentationFinite k (A ⧸ TwoSidedIdeal.asIdeal I)
